title: Summer Games
build: The PAL G64 of Epyx's disk (directory "SUMMER GAMES"): the boot file SUMMER GAMES and SGLOAD, the engine B unpacked to $0C00-$3EFF, the opening ceremony A, six event files D, E, F, H, I and K each unpacked over $4000 upward (swimming over $1000-$BEFF), the world records WR and DEFAULT, and the unused files L and M; a second PAL image and an NTSC image were supplied too

records.c: The vault's entry (module 7): screen off, raster lines for PAL or NTSC, the KERNAL switched out ($01 = $05) with NMI and IRQ vectors in RAM, then copies the picture: screen colours $B740 to $C000, colour RAM $BB28 to $D800, and the bitmap $9800-$B6FF to $E000

Sets parts of the screen and bitmap the copy leaves, the sprites' colours, single colour and unexpanded, VIC bank 3 (screen $C000, bitmap $E000), the background from gym_bg, and the number of vaulters: the players, or 8 in practice
The interrupt on line $FB through $FFFE to gym_irq, bitmap mode on, row 24 of the screen colours set to white on black for the text line, the sprite data areas cleared
Each vault: sprites off, pointers $10-$15, the gymnast at X $19 and Y $AE in frame 0, run speed 3. On the second vault of a turn straight to the run
Practice: prints "SCORE:" and its value
Competition: writes the last gymnast's total into the record, then takes the next player down; after the first the event ends with "PUSH BUTTON TO CONTINUE" and back to the engine's menu at $0900
Prints the gymnast's name on the text line and blanks the rest
The score board's digits start blank, the score in $38 at $45 (6.9)
Waits for the fire button to be let go, then for it to be held eight frames ("get set"): the gymnast takes the set pose; letting go starts the run

The run-up: the run's frames ($02-$0E) a step every three frames, X up three a step, footsteps at frames 7 and 13; the track rises and falls under the gymnast at X $59 and $98. Pressing fire again from X $7E jumps for the springboard; reaching X $B5 first is a miss
A miss: the gymnast stops; miss_count counts it and the button starts again
The hurdle onto the springboard: from X $3C-$5F the board is met at Y $AF, otherwise at $B1, too low. The gymnast rises and comes down onto it
The board's Y the hurdle comes down to: $AF for a good take-off, $B1 for a poor one

On the board: X moves on ten; landing outside X $78-$91 is a miss. Otherwise the spring: the height reached ($1C) is $99 plus a quarter of how far short of $92 the board was met; a stick pushed left or right gives the half twist (frames from $7B, one more for the difficulty)
The flight speed's base, $C4, or $BC with the twist
The flight to the horse: rises with the frames until the hands reach it
Waits a frame, leaving for the push-off at once when fire is pressed
On the horse: the hands sound, then the body turns over the hands a frame at a time, down and then up again, waiting for the fire button
The frame at which the body has come down onto the hands, set when the hands reach the horse
The frame at which the body has come back up off the hands

The push: the frames the body had turned before fire was pressed ($37) take X back by push_table, so the earlier press in the turn moves the gymnast less far back. The flight frames start from there: twisted ($22) or not
The flight: Y rises a pixel each time the gravity count (gravity_table by height) runs out, until the apex at $1C, then falls, by rewriting four DEC instructions as INC. Each step the stick is read
Stick up: the tuck, its frames $1C on and a quarter of the frames per turn; stick centred again: back to the layout, four times slower
Turns a frame; passing frames $2B, $47, $96 and $B2 (each half turn in each position) adds one to the difficulty
Between turns, the drift forward on odd gravity counts
Stick down: the landing pose, its own frames, turning slowly; letting go returns to the turn
A landing leaning forward: a tenth off, then 31 frames to push the stick back (bit 3) to stand up; otherwise 1.5 back and then the fall's 3.0 off
A landing leaning back: a tenth off, the stick forward (bit 2) to recover; otherwise 1.5 back and the fall
Recovered from the lean: the arms-up pose
A clean landing: the gymnast settles to the mat; a stick pushed either way in the next 31 frames tips the landing into a lean
The arms-up finish, the score and the crowd
A fall: the body lands at its angle, 3.0 off the score ($1E tenths from $38), a thud
The gymnast walks off to the right, footsteps, then the next vault
One gravity step of the flight in the layout or tuck, with the landing test: on reaching the mat (Y $C2) at an angle land_height says is too low, a fall
The DEC, rewritten to INC at the apex, that moves Y up and then down (layout and tuck)
The DEC or INC (rewritten) of the gravity index in the layout and tuck; then the next count and the landing test
One gravity step in the landing pose: on the mat the body's angle sorts the landing: forward lean, clean, back lean, or past them a fall
The same DEC or INC of Y in the landing pose
The DEC or INC (rewritten) that steps the gravity count's index in the landing pose; then the next count, and the landing test on the mat by the body's angle
The miss sound; the second miss in a turn ends it with no score
The first miss: the score board shows dashes
Draws a score digit four cells wide into the bitmap's score board from big_digit_l and big_digit_r: digit X at position Y
Puts the gymnast standing on the mat, facing the way of the vault
Moves the body down $16 and on $20 for the mat
A footstep: voice 1 noise
The springboard's twang: voice 2
The miss buzzer: voice 3, held 16 frames twice
The hands on the horse: voice 2
The crowd: two noise voices swelling, longer for a score of 10.0 or more
The fall's thud

The score in tenths at $38: less the frames spent in the landing pose ($25), plus 0.8 for each half turn and twist ($22), less twice how far the spring's height fell short ($1C - $9F), at least 0; shown in the big digits as d.d, or 10.0 and more with a "1"
Adds the two vaults and writes the total into the player's record: three score bytes and the text "dd.d"; waits for fire
Turns the score into text "dd.d" at $10-$13 and prints it on the text line
Waits X frames, by the raster lines at $2A and $33
Moves the animation frame on by A; past the end of the loop ($4CF8) it goes back to the start ($4CFC). Then X moves on by the speed ($4D08)
The frame after the loop's last
The first frame of the animation loop
Adds the speed to the gymnast's X, nine bits
The run speed, X's step per frame: 3 on the run, set again for the flight
Mirrors the unpacked shape at $3B left to right, through bit_reverse
Stores the unpacked shape upside down into the sprite buffer
The buffer's low byte in flip_store's first store
The buffer's high byte in flip_store's first store
The buffer's low byte in flip_store's second store
The buffer's high byte in flip_store's second store
The buffer's low byte in flip_store's third store
The buffer's high byte in flip_store's third store

Draws animation frame $1F/$20: each frame has 20 bytes in frame_table, six shapes and a flags byte. Each shape is unpacked (a count of leading zero bytes, then the rest) into $3B and copied into the back buffer ($C400 or $C600), mirrored or flipped as the flags say; then places the sprites
The next shape of the frame
The low byte of the buffer address the shape is copied to
The sprite buffer's high byte for the shape being copied ($C4 or $C6)
Waits for line $34, then sets the six sprites' X and Y from the frame's offsets around the gymnast's X and Y, with the high X bits, and flips the pointers to the buffer just drawn
The raster interrupt: alternates lines $F2 and $FB, turning multicolour off for the text line and on again above it
Prints character A on the text line at column X: copies its eight bytes from the character ROM into the bitmap's last row, with the ROM switched in
Each byte with its bits reversed, for mirror_rows
"      SCORE:"
"TOTAL SCORE:"
"        PUSH BUTTON TO CONTINUE         "
The score board's bytes for blank and dashes
Where the four score digits go in the bitmap
The score board's digits, left halves, 16 bytes each
The digits' right halves
Frames per pixel of rise or fall by distance from the apex
How far X moves back at the push, by the frames turned on the hands before fire: $FF (one forward) at once, then $18 falling to 0
The lowest Y the body may reach on the mat, by its angle, in the layout and tuck
The same for the landing pose, facing one way
And facing the other way
Low bytes of the 206 packed shapes' addresses
High bytes of the packed shapes' addresses
The animation frames, 20 bytes each: X and Y offsets for six sprites, six shape numbers, flags (bit 7 mirror, bit 6 upside down, low nibble the table)
Frame records continued
Frame records, from about frame 92
Frame records, from about frame 143
Frame records continued to $67FF
The 206 packed sprite shapes ($6800-$8A97): each a count of leading zero bytes, then its remaining bytes
Packed shapes
Packed shapes from $7000
Packed shapes from $7400
Packed shapes from $7800
Packed shapes from $7C00
Packed shapes from $8000
Packed shapes from $8400
Packed shapes to $8A97
Zero bytes up to the bitmap
Zero bytes
Zero bytes, the third kilobyte of the gap
Zero bytes to $97FF
The hall's bitmap, copied to $E000: the run-up, springboard, horse, mat, crowd and score board. Rows 0-2
Bitmap rows 3-5
Bitmap rows 6-8
Bitmap row 8 from $A000 onwards, to row 9
Bitmap rows 9-11
Bitmap rows 12-14
Bitmap rows 15-17
Bitmap rows 18-20
Bitmap rows 21-23
Bitmap row 24, the text line
64 bytes of $FF after the bitmap that nothing copies
The screen colours, copied to $C000: two colours per cell
The colour RAM's contents, copied to $D800 (the copy overlaps the screen colours' last 24 bytes)
The background colour
The module's last byte
